source_context: The human supplied a 19 August 2026 status report about Hermite--Lindemann and asked the agent to attempt a related LeanFrontier submission without duplicating the active upstream work. The agent selected the formal statement and wrote its proof. The pinned Mathlib release does not export Hermite--Lindemann. Upstream mathlib PR #28013 was inspected at commit 8bc69dbf4e88f329c510e4e5a493584affa19371: its Basic.lean states transcendental_exp, transcendental_e, transcendental_pi and transcendental_log, but it does not state this Set.InjOn result. No source or proof from that pull request is copied here. Instead, the entrypoint takes the exponential Hermite--Lindemann theorem as an explicit premise and derives that Complex.exp is injective on the set of algebraic complex numbers: equality of the exponentials makes exp (a - b) equal to one, while Hermite--Lindemann makes that value transcendental if a and b are distinct. The theorem will be directly instantiable when transcendental_exp is available from a released Mathlib. This is a classical corollary and is not claimed as new mathematics. A private batch probe against rfl, simp, norm_num, tauto, omega and decide failed for every tactic before submission.
